body:
## Pull request overview

Deprecates the redundant `IUIService` contract and consolidates UI metadata access into `IMetadataService`, adding UI convenience methods and extending `getEffective()` to accept optional auth context for user-scoped overlay resolution. Updates docs/plans/roadmap to reflect the migration.

**Changes:**
- Mark `IUIService` as `@deprecated` and document migration to `IMetadataService`.
- Add UI convenience methods (`getView`, `listViews`, `getDashboard`, `listDashboards`) and extend `getEffective()` with optional auth context.
- Implement + test the new `IMetadataService` behaviors in `MetadataManager`, and update docs/roadmap/dispatcher notes accordingly.

### Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 10 out of 10 changed files in this pull request and generated 5 comments.

| packages/spec/src/api/dispatcher.zod.ts | Annotates `/api/v1/ui` route as deprecated in favor of metadata routes. |

| packages/spec/API_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md | Replaces `plugin-ui-api` plan with metadata API equivalents and endpoints. |

| content/docs/guides/contracts/metadata-service.mdx | Adds “UI Metadata” section and overlay/customization examples. |
| ROADMAP.md | Marks `IUIService` deprecated and updates plan items accordingly. |
</details>

The `@deprecated` migration examples recommend `metadata.listViews(...)`/`metadata.getView(...)`, but in the updated `IMetadataService` contract those methods are optional. To avoid forcing consumers into unsafe calls/casts, consider updating this deprecation JSDoc to recommend the guaranteed APIs (`metadata.get('view', name)`, `metadata.list('view')`, etc.) and mention the convenience methods only as optional helpers.
```suggestion
 *
 * Recommended migration targets (guaranteed APIs):
 * - getView(name) → metadata.get('view', name)
 * - listViews(object?) → metadata.list('view', { object })
 * - registerView(name, def) → metadata.register('view', name, def)
 * - getDashboard(name) → metadata.get('dashboard', name)
 * - listDashboards() → metadata.list('dashboard')
 * - registerDashboard(name, def) → metadata.register('dashboard', name, def)
 *
 * Optional convenience helpers (only if your IMetadataService implementation exposes them):
 * - metadata.getView?.(name)
 * - metadata.listViews?.(object)
 * - metadata.getDashboard?.(name)
 * - metadata.listDashboards?.()
 * - metadata.registerView?.(name, def)
 * - metadata.registerDashboard?.(name, def)
 *
```

The stub’s header comment says it “delegates to IMetadataService when available”, but this implementation is purely an in-memory `Map` and does not delegate. Either adjust the comment to match behavior, or implement actual delegation (e.g., if the dev kernel has a `metadata` service, forward `getView`/`listViews`/etc. to it).

This doc uses `metadataService.listViews('account')` / `getEffective(..., { userId })` as the primary UI examples. Since `listViews()` is optional in the `IMetadataService` contract, readers may not be able to call it safely on all implementations. Consider either switching the examples to `metadataService.list('view')` + filtering, or explicitly stating that `listViews()`/`getView()` are convenience helpers provided by `MetadataManager` (and may not exist on every `IMetadataService`).

`getEffective()` tries to load a user-specific overlay via `this.overlayKey(..., 'user') + ":${context.userId}"`, but `overlayKey()`/`saveOverlay()` currently key overlays only by `type:name:scope` (no `owner`). As a result this lookup can never succeed, and—more importantly—it's impossible to store more than one user overlay per item because user overlays will overwrite each other. Consider incorporating `owner` into the storage key for `scope==='user'` (and updating `getOverlay`/`saveOverlay`/`removeOverlay` accordingly, plus a test that saves overlays for two different users and resolves each correctly).
